newsitem.title: UK: Germany could cut Eurofighter order - paper.
newsitem.headline: Germany could cut Eurofighter order - paper.

text.p: Germany may cut back its order for the Eurofighter jet by 22 percent to save four billion Deutsche marks, said a report in The Times on Monday attributing the remarks to the defence minister Volker Ruhe while on a trip to India.

The report said that the German minister indicated he would cut the order to 140 planes from 180 to meet tough budget constraints. "Everyone has budget cuts. France has, Great Britain has, Germany has..I will negotiate the quesiton of money we can use for the Eurofighter in the next four years until I have satisfactory results.
"I can only spend the money I have," he said in The Times report.
But the newspaper report added that the German defence ministry officials later denied the German order would be cut.

Germany has come under pressure recently to make a decision on its order. This follows Spain announcing its order for 87 aircraft last week. Britain was the first to step forward and say it would buy 232 aircraft out of a total production run of 620.
The Eurofighter is to be built by a consortium comprising British Aerospace Plc, Germany's Daimler-Benz AG unit Dasa, Alenia SpA of Italy and Spain's CASA.
